HEADER:
Date: 2025-04-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (AtlasHealth Cloud Eng), Ben Ortiz (AtlasHealth ML Eng), Samir Patel (AtlasHealth SRE)
---
SUMMARY: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing rollout plan for pilot -> production cutover. Topics: canary strategy, A/B split, monitoring & runbooks, rollback criteria, maintenance window and stakeholders. Next steps and owners captured.
TOPICS: canary rollout, cutover window, metrics and alerts, runbook walk, performance expectations, data residency/KMS note
ACTION ITEMS: see metadata field above for structured list

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Alyssa: all right almost on time, hi everyone thanks for joining, this is the AtlasHealth pilot cutover planning sync. I'm Alyssa from Redwood, and Marco is our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya: doing well thanks, busy week but ready to lock this down.
[00:15] Marco: hey all, quick agenda: confirm canary window, define A/B percentages, monitoring/alerts, runbook owners, and final prerequisites for cutover.
[00:22] Ben: sounds good. We ran the last inference bench yesterday, quantization looked stable but we saw a p95 spike at longer contexts.
[00:30] Marco: noted. That's likely the KV-cache warmup for long sequences; option to pre-warm cache or run a small warmup traffic ramp. We'll show the warmup snippet in the runbook.
[00:40] Priya: main constraint for us is a strict 2-hour maintenance window on Saturday 02:00-04:00 UTC. We need to be fully back by 04:00, can't exceed.
[00:49] Alyssa: ok that's tight but doable. We'll design canary so production traffic is minimally impacted and rollback is automated.
[00:56] Samir: quick question on data residency — the pilot used hosted API but we need logs to remain in our VPC for the production staged rollout. Can we get audit logs and KMS key usage?
[01:08] Marco: yes, for Dedicated/Private we can hook into your KMS, and audit logs are shipped to your S3 in the VPC or the syslog endpoint. We'll include the exact controls in the security appendix of the runbook.
[01:20] Ben: on canary percentages — we were thinking 5% for an initial 30 minute run, then 20% for next 30, then full cutover if no issues. Thoughts?
[01:30] Alyssa: that's a reasonable ramp. My suggestion is slightly more conservative: 2% for 15 minutes to verify heat, 10% for 30 minutes, 25% for 30, then switch to 100% with a 10m observation. The important thing is automated health gates.
[01:45] Priya: automated gates meaning what exactly?
[01:50] Marco: rules we can implement in the routing layer: if error rate exceeds X OR p95 latency increases beyond threshold OR model-quality regressions detected -> automatic rollback to previous model/host pool. We'll capture thresholds in the runbook.
[02:06] Ben: for model-quality regressions, we need a golden dataset and a quick evaluation script. I can prepare a small dataset of 300 prompts and a lightweight eval that runs within 5 minutes to verify token-level quality and hallucination rate.
[02:20] Priya: good. Also, cost controls — if we see token spend spike beyond budget during canary, we want automated throttle. Is that supported?
[02:28] Marco: we can configure cost limits and route to a cheaper quantized variant or fall back to the hosted non-dedicated pool. Redwood Optimize can also set dynamic batching to reduce token cost. We'll add a cost gate: if projected 1h spend > threshold -> switch to fallback model variant.
[02:42] Alyssa: we'll capture all of that in the pre-cutover checklist.
[02:45] Samir: on monitoring / dashboards, what's the tech stack? We use Datadog and PagerDuty.
[02:51] Marco: we have Datadog metrics exports out-of-the-box (latency histograms, token counts, error rates) plus traces for cold-starts. We'll provide a dashboard JSON you can import. For PagerDuty we can push alerts via webhook; we'll recommend specific thresholds.
[03:05] Priya: please include p50/p95/p99, 5xx error rate, token/sec, and per-route cost.
[03:12] Marco: will do. We'll also include synthetic monitors that run key prompts every minute during the cutover, so you get early detection of quality regressions.
[03:22] Ben: question on routing — our app is Kubernetes-based and uses Istio. How do we set up canary? We prefer A/B at the application layer rather than changing DNS.
[03:31] Marco: two paths: you can do edge-level split via your Istio route weights to call Redwood endpoints in parallel, or we can provision a canary endpoint and you route a percentage of user traffic to it. Both work; Istio route weights give you more control within your infra. We'll provide example Istio config.
[03:47] Priya: we want to avoid double-invocation in prod, so Istio split it is. We just need clear instructions for header-based routing and retries.
[03:55] Marco: yep header-based (x-canary) and a failure-injector option for negative tests.
[04:02] Alyssa: let's walk through the runbook outline — Marco, can you narrate the high-level steps?
[04:07] Marco: sure. Step 0: Pre-cutover validations — infra checks, secret sync, KMS policies, Datadog dashboards imported, PagerDuty routes ready. Step 1: Provision canary capacity (we'll do dedicated canary pool). Step 2: Warm caches with curated prompts. Step 3: Start 2% traffic via Istio routing for 15m with health gates. Step 4: Ramp to 10% for 30m if gates pass. Step 5: Ramp to 25% for 30m. Step 6: Full cutover and 10m observation; Step 7: Post-cutover smoke test and golden-eval run. Step 8: Closeout and retrospective.
[04:42] Ben: for step 2, cache warm-up — do you have a script we can run in CI to warm the KV cache and model weights?
[04:49] Marco: yes, we have a warmup script in the repo; I'll paste a link in the runbook and show the curl commands. It does a sequence of calls that mimic long and short contexts.
[04:58] Priya: backups: if we have to roll back, what's the exact rollback time and impact? Will sessions lose state?
[05:07] Marco: rollback is a routing switch back to previous pool and model variant; sessions with long-running KV state may see a small mismatch but we have a prefix-cache persistence option and we'll document expected behavior. Recovery time targeted under 2 minutes for routing flip.
[05:21] Samir: what about keys and encryption — during cutover do we rotate any keys?
[05:26] Alyssa: not during cutover; key rotations are recommended outside maintenance windows. We'll note that as a no-op in the checklist.
[05:33] Priya: SLAs — we need to understand latency SLOs for the dedicated pool. Our internal SLA expects p95 < 300ms for the 512-token average payload. Is that feasible?
[05:44] Marco: for 512 average tokens on the dedicated pool with the model quantized to int8, p95 ~250–320ms depending on concurrency. We'll aim for 300ms threshold but add a note: higher context lengths push p95 up. We'll recommend a concurrency cap and batching config to hit p95 consistently.
[06:02] Ben: let's put concrete numbers in the runbook: target p50 90ms, p95 280ms for 512 tokens, error rate < 0.5%.
[06:10] Alyssa: agreed. We'll include those targets and the fallback behavior if the SLOs are violated.
[06:16] Priya: on auditing, legal asked for an audit trail of who triggered rollbacks and who ran golden evaluations. Can we add user-level audit logs?
[06:25] Marco: yes, we capture operator actions in the control plane and can export to your SIEM. We'll include a sample SIEM ingestion file.
[06:33] Samir: can you confirm retention window for logs? We need 13 months for compliance.
[06:39] Marco: default is 90 days but with an enterprise add-on we can extend to 13 months; I'll include pricing in the sheet.
[06:47] Priya: good. Also want to lock down the person who will hit the big red button in case of rollback.
[06:52] Alyssa: that should be an Atlas on-call SRE, Samir? and we will require two-person verification for final full cutover.
[07:00] Samir: yes Samir is on-call that weekend so I'll be primary. Ben will be quality lead.
[07:06] Ben: ok.
[07:08] Alyssa: runbook will have an explicit "who does what" matrix.
[07:12] Marco: another minor point — if you want to A/B test model variants (e.g., 1-shot vs 3-shot prompts) during canary, we can spin up parallel endpoints and do a traffic split. That helps validate cost/quality tradeoffs.
[07:25] Ben: we want to test a quantized 7B vs unquantized 13B for cost pick. We'll do that in a separate experiment but maybe during the 25% ramp we can route a slice to the 7B to compare.
[07:36] Priya: just be careful about stateful sessions mixing endpoints.
[07:40] Marco: noted, route by session ID to keep sticky sessions.
[07:43] Alyssa: ok logistics — Marco will provision canary pool and share endpoints/creds, I'll send the cost breakdown, Priya will confirm window. Any blockers on scheduling the Saturday window?
[07:54] Priya: only dependency is change control ticket — I need to attach runbook and PD rota to the ticket. If you send runbook draft by Friday morning I can get approval.
[08:04] Alyssa: we can do that. I'll aim to send runbook and checklist by Friday 09:00 UTC.
[08:10] Ben: I will prepare golden dataset and the eval harness, I'll also instrument our Istio config and share a snippet.
[08:18] Samir: I'll add the PagerDuty escalation policy and ensure the on-call is aware.
[08:22] Marco: I'll also dump a Datadog dashboard JSON and provide an import link, plus an example Istio virtualservice snippet for routing.
[08:31] Priya: any risks we're not talking about? I'm worried about rate-limit surprises from downstream APIs during the ramp.
[08:38] Marco: recommend throttle your downstream external calls with a token bucket so we don't cascade failures. We'll add that to the checklist.
[08:44] Ben: another risk is prompt drift — during pilot the model answered differently for certain clinical phrasing. Our golden-eval should include edge-case prompts to catch that.
[08:54] Alyssa: good call. We'll bake in a manual signoff after the golden-eval before full cutover.
[08:59] Priya: timeline recap?
[09:02] Alyssa: runbook + checklist to Priya by Fri 09:00 UTC, Marco will provision canary by Thurs EOD and share endpoints, Ben deliver golden dataset by Sat 00:00 UTC, Samir config PagerDuty by Fri EOD. Maintenance window Sat 02:00-04:00 UTC.
[09:18] Priya: all right that works, we'll send the change control ticket once we have the runbook.
[09:22] Alyssa: last thing — links: runbook draft (placeholder) https://redwood.link/runbooks/atlashealth-canary-draft and datadog dashboard https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/import/atlas-canary (we'll replace with final links).
[09:34] Ben: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[09:36] Marco: quick note — we'll also include a minimal smoke test suite that you can run post-cutover (curl tests + golden-eval).
[09:44] Alyssa: ok we'll circle back same time next week if anything changes; otherwise we'll be in touch Fri morning with artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[09:52] Priya: thanks all.
[09:54] Samir: thanks.
---
END OF TRANSCRIPT
